paragraphs: Buckinghamshire Council has more than 500 children and young people in its care, and it approved 42 new foster carers in 2025-26. It recruits through its own service, Foster with Bucks, and children from the county may also live with independent agencies such as those listed on this page.

Alongside its allowances, the council offers carers a perks package that includes help with the full council tax bill for eligible carers, free parking in council car parks, free bus travel in Bucks for carers and the children they look after, a free leisure centre membership, a device for fostering paperwork, and family passes to local museums and events. Carers also get 24/7 support and training.

In April 2026 the council launched a drive for therapeutic foster carers for children with the most complex needs, including young people ready to move on from residential homes. It says these carers receive enhanced training, tailored support and allowances of £48,500 to £56,000 a year, depending on the child's age. It is particularly keen to hear from people with backgrounds in health, education, SEND, emergency services or youth justice.

Foster with Bucks holds free online information evenings each month. Compare what the council offers with two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about the training, support and allowances for the type of fostering you have in mind.
